subject: System Design
title: Write-Ahead Logs
description: A quick win: understand Write-Ahead Logs.

hook.text: A database crashes mid-write. The data was half-saved. How does it recover without corruption?

buildup.text: A write-ahead log records every change before applying it. If a crash occurs, the log replays cleanly.

discovery.text: WALs are sequential writes — much faster than random writes to disk. This speeds up commits too.

twist.text: WALs also power replication. Replicas read the primary's log and apply changes in the same order.

climax.text: The write-ahead log is one of the most important data structures in all of database engineering.

punchline.text: Log the change first — then apply it safely.

quiz.question: What does a write-ahead log do?
options: Records changes before applying them for crash recovery
